statement.p: The monthly payment for a home loan is given by a function f(P,r,N) where P is the principal (the initial size of the loan), r the interest rate, and N the length of the loan in months. Interest rates are expressed as a decimal: A % interest rate is denoted by r=0.075. If P=150000, r=0.075, and N=264(a 22-year loan), then the monthly payment is f(150000,0.075,264)=1156. Furthermore, with these values we have \frac{\partial{f}}{\partial{P}}=0.0078, \quad \frac{\partial{f}}{\partial{r}}=7849, \quad \frac{\partial{f}}{\partial{N}}=-1.4359 Estimate:
(a) The change in monthly payment per 1000 increase in loan principal:
(b) The change in monthly payment if the interest rate changes from r=0.075 to r=0.065:
(c) The change in monthly payment if the length of the loan changes from 22 to 24 years:

static.solution:
f(P,r,N) is \Delta f \approx \frac{\partial{f}}{\partial{P}}\Delta P +\frac{\partial{f}}{\partial{r}}\Delta r +\frac{\partial{f}}{\partial{N}}\Delta N By the given data and assuming that \Delta P=1000, \Delta r=0 and \Delta N=0, we get \Delta f\approx 0.0078\cdot 1000=7.8 The change in monthly payment per 1000 dollar increase in loan principal is 7.8 dollars.
(b) By the given data, we have \Delta f\approx 0.0078 \Delta P + 7849 \Delta r - 1.4359 \Delta N Substituting \Delta r=-0.01, \Delta P=0 and \Delta N=0 gives: \Delta f \approx 7849 \cdot -0.01 =\2483484 -78.49
(c) We substitute \Delta N=(24-22)\cdot 12=24 months, and \Delta r=\Delta P=0 to obtain \Delta f\approx -1.4359 \cdot 24=-34.4616
